evidence_interpretation: Any amount of lead in blood means the person was exposed to lead.
limitations: A BLL establishes that lead entered the person's body but does not by itself identify the source, workplace, vessel, task, route, date of exposure, or establish that lead caused a particular symptom or illness.

evidence_interpretation: BLL is generally a good indication of recent lead exposure because lead in blood has a substantially shorter half-life than lead stored in bone.
limitations: BLL is not a complete measure of historical body burden. Lead can remain stored in bone for years to decades; a later BLL therefore cannot by itself reconstruct the source, timing, magnitude, or location of a historical occupational exposure.
